body:
SKETCH v1 for STORY-1662 is posted as a comment on the spec (`aida show STORY-1662 --comments`, the last one). No code is written; waiting for your signoff.

Summary: the BUG-2139 fresh headless arm of `aida queue work <SPEC> --no-human` already provides the process, lease, child grant and launcher-free authorship. The new work is `run_standalone_implementer`, a twin of the standalone reviewer. It provisions the punt and hold files, adds a stop-at-PR contract, spawns and waits, then prints a single `implementer:` outcome line with exit codes 0/31/32/33. It also scrubs drain env from the child. Wrapping an --auto-complete variant is ruled out because drain.lock is global. After that come the template and relay prompt rewrites, a ratchet test, and the e2e plus throughput measurement. Three PRs.

Q1 needs your ruling: when a GRANTED launcher does not delegate implementer, should the child fall back to baseline (I recommend this, since it is the TASK-1764 ask) or fail closed?
subject: SKETCH: STORY-1662
